text:
jess-people-ops: Hey everyone - quick heads up: today we're launching a pilot called the "Dependency Care Credit" for 2026. It's a small stipend to help cover care costs for dependents (elder care, ADA-related caregiving, long-term childcare beyond subsidized options). Details and a short FAQ below. Please flag any major blockers by EOD Fri. :spiral_calendar: 

jess-people-ops: TL;DR: $500/yr per eligible employee, paid as a taxable stipend via payroll in two installments. Pilot runs Jan 1 2026 through Dec 31 2026. Opt-in required via People Ops form. Eligibility is broad but region-specific limits apply (see EU/UK note). Internal doc: https://redwood.internal/hr/dependency-care-credit

aaron-people-ops: Note: this is not PTO. It's a reimbursement-style stipend for things like in-home caregivers, respite care, home-mod equipment, transportation to appointments. Not for regular household bills.

emily-hr: Eligibility checklist (summary):
- Employee status: full-time or part-time > 0.6 FTE
- Employed for at least 6 months of the pilot year
- Dependent types: child under 18, adult dependent with documented need, elderly parent receiving regular care
- Cannot double-dip with regional caregiver subsidies (see EU exceptions)

matt-cto: Who needs to sign off on payroll integration? I'd like this in before first payment run in Feb.

payroll-bot: @jess-people-ops Payroll integration checklist created: PR-2409. Next payroll cutoff: 2026-02-15.

jess-people-ops: @matt-cto Payroll will handle config (cc @payroll-bot). Aaron and I scoped tax treatment with finance for US/Canada. EU/UK needs local tax vetting.

luis-eu-ops: In EU we'll need country-by-country notes. Spain/Germany likely taxable; France may require employer reporting. I can coordinate with local counsel next week.

aaron-people-ops: FAQ for managers (paste-ready):
Q: Is this retroactive? A: No. Payments start Feb; pilot applies to expenses dated Jan 1 2026 onward.
Q: Does this impact benefits eligibility? A: No, it's additive and does not change health or leave entitlements.
Q: How to claim? A: Upload receipts to People Ops form and choose stipend payout or reimbursement.

jess-people-ops: Example receipts accepted: invoices from care providers, bank statements showing payment to certified caregivers, invoices for home modifications. Not accepted: rent, utilities, general school tuition (unless documented as care services).

emily-hr: We're scheduling a 20-min all-hands + AMA next Wed 10am PT to walk through the pilot. Invite and link to follow.

matt-cto: Any budget cap per team?

aaron-people-ops: Company cap: budget supports up to 1,200 employees. If opt-ins exceed that we will prorate based on opt-in date. Don't expect to hit it but want transparency.

luis-eu-ops: Request: local HR add a short line in EU offer letters to mention pilot availability (so new hires know they can opt in once eligible).

jess-people-ops: Action items:
- People Ops: finalize form + receipt flow (due 2026-01-20) - @aaron-people-ops
- Payroll: set up PR-2409 and tax codes (due 2026-02-05) - @payroll-bot
- EU/UK counsel: confirm tax treatment by 2026-01-28 - @luis-eu-ops
- Eng managers: remind teams about AMA and share this thread with anyone who might use it

aaron-people-ops: If anyone sees compliance red flags for specific countries DM me.

matt-cto: Will share summary in infra-all after the AMA.

jess-people-ops: Thanks team - reaction if you want to join the pilot cohort planning call next Tue 9am PT. :raised_hands: :heart:

luis-eu-ops: :raised_hands:
